Debug this query

Monzo's own Data Science hiring post says the technical interview goes through your submission: its logic, trade-offs and testing (Monzo blog — Interviewing for Data Science at Monzo (Monzo's recruiting team), 27 Apr 2026). Testing your own SQL starts with reading a query that runs, returns a plausible number, and is wrong.

The ask: How many card accounts made no transaction in March 2026? The query below runs on our card ledger and answers 0. Find the line.

1SELECT COUNT(*) AS accounts_with_no_march_spend
2FROM (
3  SELECT a.account_id, COUNT(t.txn_id) AS march_txns
4  FROM accounts a
5  LEFT JOIN transactions t ON t.account_id = a.account_id
6  WHERE t.txn_at >= '2026-03-01' AND t.txn_at < '2026-04-01'
7  GROUP BY a.account_id
8)
9WHERE march_txns = 0;
Show the bug

Line 6: a WHERE on the right table of a LEFT JOIN. An account with no March transaction joins as NULL, the WHERE drops that row, and the account can never be counted as 0. The ledger has 200 accounts and 196 of them spent in March, so the answer is 4, not 0. Move the date condition into the ON clause:

1SELECT COUNT(*) AS accounts_with_no_march_spend
2FROM (
3  SELECT a.account_id, COUNT(t.txn_id) AS march_txns
4  FROM accounts a
5  LEFT JOIN transactions t
6         ON t.account_id = a.account_id
7        AND t.txn_at >= '2026-03-01' AND t.txn_at < '2026-04-01'
8  GROUP BY a.account_id
9)
10WHERE march_txns = 0;
Fix the same bug in the app: question 336 from our Debug set, not the Monzo set All Debug questions The trap, explained

How the interview runs (sourced)

The Monzo SQL interview, as candidates report it

Monzo publishes how its data interviews run, in posts on its own blog, and this page is built from them. Each row is what Monzo, candidates and prep guides have described publicly, with its source; where sources disagree, the row says so. Formats change — treat every specific as reported, not official.

Roles where SQL is testedData Science (the take-home is written in SQL or Python) and Analytics Engineering (Monzo names its stack as dbt, BigQuery, Looker, SQL and some Python).[1][2]
Stages (Data Science, 2026)A 15-minute recruiter call, a 45-minute initial call with a senior or lead data scientist, a technical screen, then final interviews of 2–3 hours: an open-ended case study and a behavioural interview. Senior and lead roles may add a leadership interview.[1]
Where the SQL isIn the technical screen, as a take-home coding task: clear, sensible SQL or Python that answers business questions with data, done in your own time rather than live in front of a panel. Monzo lists the technical screen as one hour; the post does not say how that hour divides between the task and the interview.[1]
The reviewA technical interview with a data science manager or lead goes through the submission — its logic, trade-offs and testing — then an analytical discussion (experimentation, success metrics) and a communication part (explaining results, spotting misleading charts). Monzo says it is less about trivia than about reasoning.[1]
Time limitThe 2026 post sets none; the 2022 post says the take-home had no time limit and usually ended in a slide deck. The Analytics Engineering post gives its take-home one week.[1][3][2]
How it has changedThe 2022 post describes a ~30-minute recruiter call and a take-home presented as slides; the 2026 Data Science post a 15-minute call and a technical interview on the code. A data scientist who joined in 2022 describes his take-home as metric formulation with extensive SQL and data visualisation.[3][1][4]
EnvironmentMonzo's analytics run on BigQuery, dbt and Looker. None of the sources we could read says which tool the take-home itself is done in.[2][4]
  1. [1] Monzo blog — Interviewing for Data Science at Monzo (Monzo's recruiting team) (27 Apr 2026)
  2. [2] Monzo blog — Interviewing for Analytics Engineering at Monzo (Monzo's recruiting team) (25 May 2026)
  3. [3] Monzo blog — Data hiring at Monzo: the interview process (21 Mar 2022)
  4. [4] Monzo blog — Joining Monzo as a data scientist (first-person account) (17 May 2022)

The SQL that comes up

What Monzo SQL questions test

Reported most often, in order

  • 1Turning a stakeholder's question into a metric, then into SQL
  • 2Metrics over a period: counts, rates and ratios with GROUP BY
  • 3Readable, testable SQL you can defend line by line
  • 4Experiment and success-metric reasoning on top of the query
  • 5Data modelling into clean tables (Analytics Engineering)
  • 6Explaining a result to a non-technical reader

Difficulty: No source we could read grades it; Monzo describes the bar as clear, sensible code and sound reasoning rather than trivia, and the 2022 post set no time limit on the take-home. The data is accounts (signup date, plan, country), card transactions (merchant, category, amount, status, timestamps), transfers in and out between customers, and money moved into and out of savings pots.

Sample questions

Monzo SQL question shapes, and where to practise them

Shapes candidates and guides report (paraphrased)

  • A data request arrives in plain business language: decide what to measure, write the SQL (or Python) that answers it, and present the finding so a non-technical reader can act on it.[1]
  • Formulate a metric for an area of the product, compute it with SQL, and show it as a chart.[4]
  • In the follow-up, defend your own submission: why this join or filter, what you assumed about the data, how you checked the numbers.[1]
  • Analytics Engineering: model raw data into tables others will query, pragmatic rather than over-engineered, and explain the modelling trade-offs.[2]

Every challenge in the Monzo set, by topic

These are SQL Quest challenges matched to the topics candidates report for Monzo — not questions Monzo has asked.

Every query here runs on SQLite in your browser. Joins, GROUP BY, CTEs and window functions are written the same way in PostgreSQL, MySQL and Snowflake; dates are where they differ (SQLite's strftime('%Y-%m', ts) is to_char(ts, 'YYYY-MM') in PostgreSQL), and the app lists each difference beside every challenge.
